newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark weak after German data,Eurobourses soft.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark weak after German data,Eurobourses soft.

text.p: The dollar rose to a two-year high against the mark on Thursday after weak German data and firmed against the yen following another plunge in Tokyo stocks, sparked by worries over huge Japanese bank debts.
The three percent share tumble in Tokyo plus a 51-point drop in Wall Street did nothing to calm nerves on European bourses, where there was increased anxiety about interest rates.
London, Frankfurt and Paris were all lower in morning trading, though the Paris bourse was supported by merger rumours.

The dollar touched its new two-year high just above 1.58 marks after German data showed a surge in unemployment during December to a postwar high as well as weaker-than -expected 1996 economic growth, widening the country's budget deficit.
The figures increased speculation that German rates would be trimmed again at some stage but analysts said no cut was expected at Thursday's regular meeting of the Bundesbank council.
By mid-morning the mark had recovered slightly but was still trading at around 1.5775 to the dollar.

Another factor tending to boost the dollar over the mark was concern over the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin, who has been admitted to hospital with pneumonia. Any threat of instability in Russia tends to have a negative effect on the German currency.

The continuing freefall in Tokyo stocks, sparked by worries that major banks cannot solve their huge debt problems and broader concern about the health of the Japanese economy, weakened the yen. In morning European trading the dollar was quoted at 116.22 yen, up from 115.90 late on Wednesday.

On the equity front, leading London shares had recovered some of their losses but were still down around half a percent by 1130 GMT and dealers said the falls in Tokyo and Wall Street as well interest rate worries were damaging sentiment.
Concern that central banks in both the United States and the Britain would push short-term interest rates higher in the coming weeks soured investor appetite for equities.

"The bond markets are telling us that British interest rates need to be a half-point higher," said Richard Jeffrey, strategist at Charterhouse Tilney. "The market needs to know what will happen with rates."
Key U.S. producer price data (expected at 1330 GMT) was the main focus of market attention on Thursday ahead of Wall Street's 1430 GMT start.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast the prices, an important clue to future U.S. credit policy, to rise by 0.3 percent in December compared with a 0.4 percent increase the previous month.

In Frankfurt German shares were little moved by the German unemployment data but dealers said the the overnight weakness on Wall Street was holding the market down. The blue chip DAX index pared some of its losses but was still around third of a percent down at 1130 GMT.
It was a similar story in Paris, where dealers cited the Tokyo tumble and the Dow's 50-point drop for soft prices.
However, Societe Generale's planned purchase of Credit du Nord from Paribas kept merger interest alive and rumours were circulating over another big, unidentified, acquisition.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5775 marks and 116.22 yen compared with 1.5758 and 115.90 late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares had fallen 18.4 points to 4,069.0.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 12.21 at 2,894.13.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index dropped 4.73 to 2,326.99.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed easier at $354.50 compared with its London close of $355.75 on Wednesday. Silver was at $4.67
